DK28.6 is a specific medical diagnosis code used within the Danish healthcare system to classify chronic or unspecified gastrointestinal ulcers accompanied by both bleeding and perforation [^src1]. In the context of the national clinical quality databases, specifically the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK) managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this code plays a critical role in tracking patient safety and treatment complications [^src2]. 

Specifically, DK28.6 is utilized as one of the defining diagnostic codes for identifying the incidence of [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (severe bleeding) among patients being treated for [[atrieflimren]] [^src3]. Because patients with atrial fibrillation are frequently prescribed anticoagulant medications, they carry an elevated risk of severe bleeding events, making the precise tracking of gastrointestinal complications like those denoted by DK28.6 essential for national quality indicators [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].

The code is part of a broader, comprehensive set of ICD-10-DK diagnosis codes used to capture severe bleeding events across different anatomical systems. For instance, when calculating the incidence of severe bleeding, registries also pull data on intracranial hemorrhages (e.g., [[di60|DI60]] to [[ds066|DS066]]), other gastrointestinal bleeds (such as [[dk25-0|DK25.0]] to [[dk29-8a|DK29.8A]] and [[dk92-0|DK92.0]] to [[dk92-2|DK92.2]]), and respiratory or urinary tract bleeding (including [[dj942|DJ942]], [[dn02|DN02]], [[dr04|DR04]], and [[dr31|DR31]]) [^src1]. By standardizing these codes across annual reports from 2023 through 2025, the Danish health authorities ensure consistent, comparable monitoring of severe adverse events in the atrial fibrillation patient population [^src1] [^src2] [^src3].

## Claims
